definition: The small raised number in a power, also called the power or exponent, which, when it is a positive whole number, says how many copies of the base to multiply: in $2^{5}$ the index is $5$.
The rules for powers of the same base, also called the laws of indices: $a^{m} \times a^{n} = a^{m+n}$, $a^{m} \div a^{n} = a^{m-n}$ and $(a^{m})^{n} = a^{mn}$.
An index below zero, which means the reciprocal of the positive power: $a^{-n} = \frac{1}{a^{n}}$ for $a \ne 0$, so $5^{-2} = \frac{1}{25}$.
An index that is a fraction, which means a root: for $a > 0$, $a^{\frac{1}{n}} = \sqrt[n]{a}$ and $a^{\frac{m}{n}} = (\sqrt[n]{a})^{m}$, so $8^{\frac{1}{3}} = 2$.
